passages.title: Meeting Room 3
passages.text:
MEETING ROOM 3
This room is booked for the sales team every Tuesday from 9 to 11 a.m. If you need it at any other time, please write your name and the time on the list at reception, not on this door.

passages.title: Message from Priya
passages.text:
Tom – the printer on our floor has broken down again and the engineer can't come until Thursday. Until then, please use the one on the second floor, but remember it only prints in black and white.
Priya

passages.title: Staff kitchen
passages.text:
STAFF KITCHEN
The fridge will be cleaned on Friday at 4 p.m. Any food or drink without a name on it will be thrown away, but items with a name label can stay.

passages.title: Email from IT
passages.text:
To: All staff
From: Maria (IT)
The office Wi-Fi password is changing on Monday. Everyone will receive the new password by text message early on Monday morning. Please don't ask reception for it, as they won't have it.

passages.title: Note for Jack
passages.text:
Jack – Mr Evans from Greenfield Ltd phoned at 10.30. He can't come to this afternoon's meeting and would like to move it to tomorrow at the same time. Could you call him back to confirm?
Sam

questions.question: What does the notice say?
options: a) The sales team must write their names on the door of the room.
b) Anyone can use this room on Tuesday mornings if it is empty.
c) People who want the room at other times should book it at reception.
questions.explanation: The notice says 'If you need it at any other time, please write your name and the time on the list at reception'. The room is booked for the sales team on Tuesday mornings, so it is not free for anyone then, and names should go on the reception list, 'not on this door'.

questions.question: Why has Priya written to Tom?
options: a) To warn him that colour printing is no longer possible in the office
b) To tell him where he can print until the printer is repaired
c) To ask him to contact the engineer before Thursday
questions.explanation: Priya writes 'Until then, please use the one on the second floor', so she is telling Tom which printer to use until the engineer comes. She does not ask him to contact the engineer, and she only says the second-floor printer is black and white, not that colour printing is impossible for good.

questions.question: What should staff do?
options: a) Stay out of the kitchen while the fridge is being cleaned.
b) Clean the fridge themselves on Friday at 4 p.m.
c) Put a name label on any food they want to keep.
questions.explanation: The notice says food 'without a name on it will be thrown away' and 'items with a name label can stay', so staff should label food they want to keep. The kitchen is not closed, and the notice says the fridge 'will be cleaned', not that staff must clean it.

questions.question: How will staff get the new Wi-Fi password?
options: a) They will be sent it in a text message.
b) They can collect it from reception on Monday.
c) They have to choose a new one before Monday.
questions.explanation: Maria writes 'Everyone will receive the new password by text message early on Monday morning'. She says reception 'won't have it', and staff do not choose the password themselves.

questions.question: What does Jack need to do?
options: a) Phone Mr Evans to confirm the new meeting time
b) Tell Mr Evans that the meeting will start later this afternoon
c) Wait for Mr Evans to phone again later today
questions.explanation: Sam writes 'Could you call him back to confirm?' after explaining that Mr Evans wants to move the meeting to tomorrow at the same time. So Jack must phone Mr Evans; he is not asked to wait for another call, and the meeting is moving to tomorrow, not starting later today.
